articles.headline: Hong Kong's IPO Boom Faces a Cornerstone Investor Cold-Feet Problem
articles.summary_html:
Hong Kong's red-hot IPO market, on track for its strongest year in over a decade, is showing cracks as cornerstone investorslarge investors who agree in advance to buy a fixed stake in a new share listing基礎投資者 grow hesitant about committing to new listings. More than 60 per cent of companies that went public in the third quarter are now trading below their offer priceat a lower price than the one investors first paid when the shares were issued跌穿發售價, prompting institutional backers who had verbally agreed to anchorto provide a stable, reassuring commitment that supports something坐鎮；穩住 upcoming deals to quietly withdraw, forcing at least one planned October listing to be delayed until next month at the earliest.

The retreat strikes at the heart of a financing model Hong Kong's exchange has leaned on for decades. Cornerstone investors typically commit to buying a fixed stake before a listing even opens to the public, a move meant to reassure skittish retail buyers that deep-pocketedhaving a large amount of money available to spend or invest財力雄厚 names stand behind the deal. Without that early vote of confidence, underwritersfinancial institutions that help arrange and guarantee the sale of new shares包銷商 must work harder to drum up demand, and issuers risk pricing their shares lower just to get a deal done at all, a trade-off that can dent the very enthusiasm cornerstone investors were meant to generate in the first place.

Regulators, wary of a different kind of problem, have separately cracked down on what they call IPO-rigging syndicatescoordinated groups accused of illegally manipulating demand for a new share listing新股造假集團, suspending trading in one stock and restricting dealing in roughly HK$4.7 billion of assets held across 31 brokerages. Officials insist the two trends are not directly connected, but together they complicate an already delicate balancing act: keeping Hong Kong's listing pipelinethe series of companies preparing to go public in the near future上市項目儲備 attractive to global capital while weeding out the kind of inflated demanddemand that appears artificially larger than it actually is虛增需求 that can leave ordinary investors holding an overpriced stake.
articles.summary_zh_html:
香港熾熱的新股市場原本有望創下逾十年以來最佳全年表現，但隨着基礎投資者對認購新上市公司漸趨猶豫，市場已開始出現裂痕。第三季掛牌的公司中，逾六成股價已跌穿發售價，促使早前口頭答應坐鎮上市交易的機構投資者悄悄退出，導致至少一宗原定十月上市的計劃需延至最快下月進行。

這波退潮正衝擊香港交易所數十年來一直倚賴的融資模式核心。基礎投資者一般會在上市公開認購前，承諾購入固定股份，目的是向容易動搖的散戶投資者保證，有財力雄厚的機構在背後撐腰。失去這份初始信心保證，包銷商便須更費力地招攬需求，而發行人亦可能要壓低定價，才能完成交易——但這種取捨，恰恰可能削弱基礎投資者原本應該帶來的那份信心。

監管機構則另有顧慮，近日打擊所謂的新股造假集團，暫停一隻股份的交易，並限制涉及31間經紀行、約47億港元資產的交易活動。官方強調兩者並無直接關連，但兩股趨勢同時出現，令本已微妙的平衡更形複雜：既要維持香港上市項目儲備對全球資金的吸引力，同時亦要剔除可能令普通投資者高價接貨的虛增需求。
articles.image_scene: A hushed Hong Kong Stock Exchange screen room with large digital boards flashing red falling share prices, besuited bankers in a glass-walled meeting room nearby looking tense over documents, Central's skyscrapers visible through floor-to-ceiling windows.

articles.headline: Over 1,000 Hongkongers to Trial Baidu's Robotaxis in City-First Public Scheme
articles.summary_html:
Baidu's self-driving unit, Apollo Go, has opened what the company calls Hong Kong's first large-scale public triala real-world test open to ordinary members of the public, not just engineers公眾試驗 of autonomous vehiclesvehicles that can drive themselves without a human controlling the steering自動駕駛車輛, offering more than 1,000 Tung Chung residents a free ride between 21 October and 3 November. Riders travel a 5.1-kilometre designated routea specific path officially approved for a particular use指定路線 that starts near Yat Tung Estate, passes a hotel, and loops back to the start, with each trip lasting roughly 15 minutes. Tickets, distributed through the Islands District Council Secretariat, are capped at 600, enough for up to 1,200 passenger journeys since each car carries at most two riders.

Unlike a fully commercial service, every vehicle still carries a safety operatora trained person who sits in a self-driving vehicle ready to intervene if something goes wrong安全員 in the driver's seat, a reminder that the technology remains firmly in testing. Baidu says each operator has roughly a decade of driving experience and at least 100 hours of dedicated autonomous-driving training. Passengers are asked to fill in feedback questionnaires after each journey, data the company will use to fine-tune its ride-hailinga service that matches passengers with vehicles for hire, usually booked through an app網約車 algorithms before seeking approval for a wider rollout. Officials note the vehicles currently lack barrier-free facilities, underlining how far the project still sits from a full commercial launch.

The trial fits into a broader, cautious strategy by Hong Kong's Transport Department, which has gradually expanded test routes for autonomous vehicles across Lantau since 2024 rather than approving a sudden commercial rolloutthe full-scale public launch of a product or service for ordinary paying customers商業化推出. Supporters argue the staged approach lets engineers iron out safety issues before robotaxis share the road with pedestrians and cyclists at scale. Sceptics, including some in the taxi and minibus trades, worry that even a modest pilot scheme signals the eventual displacement of professional driversthe replacing of human workers in a job by machines or technology專業司機被取代, a tension likely to sharpen as the technology matures.
articles.summary_zh_html:
百度旗下自動駕駛部門「Apollo Go」在香港展開該公司稱為全港首個大型公眾試驗的自動駕駛車輛計劃，由10月21日至11月3日，向逾千名東涌居民提供免費試乘。乘客可沿一條全長5.1公里的指定路線行駛，路線由映灣園一帶出發，經過一間酒店後折返起點，全程約需15分鐘。車票經離島區議會秘書處派發，數量限於600張，由於每輛車最多可載兩位乘客，故合共可供約1,200人次試乘。

與全面商業服務不同，每輛車仍設有安全員坐在司機座位，提醒公眾這項技術仍處於測試階段。百度表示，每位安全員均具備約十年駕駛經驗，並接受最少100小時的自動駕駛專項訓練。乘客需於每程完結後填寫意見問卷，公司將利用相關數據優化其網約車演算法，然後才會申請擴大推行範圍。有關方面指出，現時車輛尚未設有無障礙設施，顯示計劃距離全面商業啟動仍有一段路。

今次試驗屬於運輸署一套較審慎的整體策略的一部分，該署自2024年起逐步擴大大嶼山一帶的自動駕駛測試路線，而非一下子批准商業化推出。支持者認為，循序漸進的做法讓工程師可在無人駕駛的士大規模與行人及單車使用者共用道路之前，先解決安全問題。然而，包括部分的士及小巴業界人士的質疑者擔心，即使是規模有限的試驗計劃，也預示着專業司機被取代的終局，隨着技術日趨成熟，這種張力相信會愈趨明顯。

articles.headline: Art or Box Office? Hong Kong Rethinks How It Funds Its Top Arts Groups
articles.summary_html:
Hong Kong is preparing to overhaul how it funds its nine flagship performing arts groups, shifting away from what has long been a near-automatic annual subsidymoney given by the government to support an organisation's running costs資助 towards a more flexible, merit-based system. Under the proposed changes, announced as part of a wider cultural policy review, the government will inject HK$200 million into the Arts and Sport Development Fund while introducing an in-and-out mechanisma system that allows organisations to gain or lose funded status depending on their performance能上能落機制 tied to artistic standards rather than guaranteed continuity.

The change is designed to free up room, and public money, for emerging companiesorganisations that are newly established or still building a reputation新興藝團 that have long struggled to compete with established institutions for recognition and resources. Yet the proposal immediately raises a thorny question: how exactly should officials measure artistic meritthe quality or value of a creative work, judged by its artistic rather than commercial success藝術價值 in a field where critical acclaim and box-office returnsthe amount of money a performance earns from ticket sales票房收入 frequently point in opposite directions? A daring, experimental production might win prizes while playing to half-empty houses, whereas a crowd-pleasing commercial hit may contribute little to the city's artistic reputation.

Directors of the nine designated groups, which include leading orchestras, dance and opera companies, have voiced cautious support paired with concern. They note that a prolonged economic downturn has made private fundraisingthe raising of money from businesses or individuals rather than the government私人集資 harder than at any point in recent memory, and have urged policymakers to set realistic targets and take a long-term view rather than judging companies on a single disappointing season. The Culture, Sports and Tourism Bureau says a fuller framework for assessing performance, including a review of venue-booking rules, will follow in the coming months, alongside wider consultation with practitioners across dance, theatre, music and Cantonese opera before any final criteria are locked in.
articles.summary_zh_html:
香港正準備全面革新資助九個旗艦表演藝術團體的方式，由一直以來近乎自動發放的年度資助，轉向較具彈性、以表現為本的制度。作為更廣泛文化政策檢討的一部分，政府將向藝術及體育發展基金注資二億港元，同時引入與藝術水平而非保證延續性掛鈎的能上能落機制。

這項改變旨在為長期難與主流機構爭奪認受及資源的新興藝團騰出空間及公共資源。然而，建議隨即引出一個棘手問題：當局究竟應如何衡量藝術價值，尤其是在藝評口碑與票房收入往往背道而馳的藝壇之中？一部大膽前衛的作品，或許能贏盡獎項卻門票只售出一半；相反，一部迎合大眾口味的商業鉅製，對本港藝術聲譽的貢獻卻可能相當有限。

九個指定藝團（包括多個主要樂團、舞團及歌劇團）的總監均表示審慎支持，但同時有所保留。他們指出，持續的經濟低迷令私人集資比近年任何時候都更加困難，並促請政策制定者訂立切合實際的目標，以長遠角度看待問題，而非單憑一季表現欠佳便作出判斷。文化體育及旅遊局表示，一套更完整的表現評估框架，包括場地租用制度的檢討，將於未來數月內公布，並會在落實最終準則前，就舞蹈、戲劇、音樂及粵劇等不同範疇，與業界人士展開更廣泛的諮詢。

articles.headline: Elderly Woman's Death Sparks Calls to Better Support and Monitor Carers
articles.summary_html:
The death of a 93-year-old Kai Tak woman last week, after her live-in domestic helper was arrested on suspicion of assault, has reopened a painful debate about how Hong Kong supports the carers of its most isolated elderly residentsolder people with little regular contact with family, neighbours or social services孤身無援長者. The victim, who had lived alone and needed round-the-clock carecontinuous care provided at all hours of the day and night全天候照顧 after a stroke, had relied almost entirely on one helper for years. Lawmakers and welfare groups say the case, however it is ultimately resolved in court, exposes a wider gap in how the city monitors households where an elderly person's wellbeing rests on a single, often overstretched carer.

Among the proposals gaining traction is expanding an existing at-risk databasea record used by authorities to flag people who may need extra support or monitoring高風險個案資料庫, through which the Hospital Authority already alerts the Social Welfare Department when listed carers are hospitalised, to cover domestic helpers caring for seniors as well. Advocates also want regular home visits and encouragement for carers to attend community centres, so that a third partysomeone outside the immediate household who can observe a situation objectively第三方 has a chance to notice warning signs before a crisis develops. Migrant workers' groups add that many helpers shoulder years of caregiving with little rest, training or outside support.

At the heart of the discussion lies a harder question for Hong Kong families: whether society does enough to prevent caregiver burnoutextreme physical and emotional exhaustion caused by prolonged, unsupported caregiving照顧者身心俱疲, whether the carer is a relative or a hired helper, before exhaustion curdles into harm. With Hong Kong's population ageing rapidly, advocates argue that expanding respite careshort-term relief care that gives a regular carer a break from caregiving duties暫託照顧服務 and community support networks is no longer optional, but essential to protecting both elderly residents and the people who care for them.
articles.summary_zh_html:
上週，啟德一名93歲女子在其同住外傭因涉嫌襲擊而被捕後死亡，事件再次觸發社會對香港如何支援照顧孤身無援長者的照顧者這一沉重議題的討論。死者獨居多年，中風後需要全天候照顧，多年來幾乎完全依賴一名外傭照料。立法會議員及福利團體指出，無論案件最終在法庭上如何判決，事件都暴露出本港在監察那些長者福祉僅繫於單一、往往不勝負荷的照顧者的家庭方面，存在明顯缺口。

目前獲得較多支持的建議之一，是擴大現有的高風險個案資料庫——醫院管理局目前已會在資料庫所列的照顧者入院時，通知社會福利署——將照顧長者的外傭亦納入其中。倡議者亦希望加強定期家訪，並鼓勵照顧者多到社區中心，讓第三方有機會在危機發生前察覺警號。外勞團體則補充，不少外傭在缺乏休息、培訓及外界支援的情況下，長年肩負照顧重擔。

討論的核心，是香港家庭一個更難回答的問題：社會是否做得足夠，去防止照顧者身心俱疲——不論照顧者是家人還是聘請的外傭——在筋疲力竭演變成傷害之前及時介入。隨著香港人口急速老化，倡議者認為，擴大暫託照顧服務及社區支援網絡已不再是可有可無，而是保護長者與照顧者雙方的必要之舉。
articles.image_scene: A quiet Hong Kong public housing estate corridor in late-afternoon light, an empty wheelchair parked outside a closed flat door, a social worker with a clipboard speaking gently to a neighbour in the hallway; no people in distress, nothing graphic shown.

trends.headline: 📱 Filmed Without Asking: MTR Livestream Sparks a Privacy Backlash
trends.summary_html:
A Hong Kong commuter's social media post has ignited a wave of anger this week after she accused a Douyin livestreamer of filming seated MTR passengers without their consentpermission freely given for something to happen同意, broadcasting their faces to an account with more than 1,000 followers. According to her account, which quickly spread across Threads, the streamer kept the camera rolling even after a passenger objected, continuing to talk loudly on the phone throughout the journey. The account in question mostly posts cheerful, slice-of-life clips of Hong Kong food and daily routines, the kind of content that has turned ordinary commutes into unpaid backdrops for someone else's content hustlethe effort of constantly producing material, often for money or attention內容創作搏殺.

The backlash reflects growing unease over where exactly the boundary sits between public space and private bystanders'people who happen to be nearby when something is filmed, without choosing to take part途人；旁觀者 dignity. Commenters have pointed out that MTR by-laws already restrict obstructive filming, yet enforcement rarely keeps pace with the sheer volume of creators chasing engagementlikes, comments, shares and other signs that an audience is reacting to content互動反應 across platforms. Some see the public shaming of the streamer online as a healthy form of accountability; others worry it is an imperfect substitutesomething used in place of a proper solution, even though it does not fully solve the problem並不完美的替代方案 for actual regulatory enforcement.
trends.summary_zh_html:
本週，一名香港乘客在社交媒體發文，指控一名抖音直播主未經車廂內乘客同意便進行拍攝，並將他們的樣貌直播給一個擁有逾千名粉絲的帳戶，貼文迅速在Threads瘋傳，引發廣泛不滿。根據她的描述，即使有乘客表示反對，該直播主仍繼續開着鏡頭，並在全程大聲講電話。涉事帳戶主要發佈輕鬆的香港飲食及日常生活片段，這類內容正把尋常的通勤變成別人內容創作搏殺的免費場景。

這場反彈反映出公眾日益關注公共空間與途人個人尊嚴之間的界線應劃在何處。有網民指出，港鐵附例本已限制妨礙性拍攝行為，但執法往往追不上各平台創作者為追逐互動反應而不斷湧現的拍攝風潮。有人認為網上公開指責該直播主，是一種健康的問責方式；但亦有人擔心，這只是對真正監管執法的並不完美的替代方案。

causes.label: Consent as the Missing Norm in Platform Culture
causes.label_zh: 同意：平台文化中缺失的準則
causes.text: Livestreaming turns any public space into a potential stage, but the people who happen to be nearby rarely get a say in whether their face ends up online. Students could ask whether Hong Kong's privacy rules, written for an earlier media era, still adequately protect bystanders who never agreed to appear in someone else's content.
causes.text_zh: 直播把任何公共空間都變成潛在舞台，但碰巧身處現場的人卻幾乎沒有機會決定自己的樣貌是否要在網上曝光。學生可以探討，香港那些為舊時代媒體而設的私隱規例，是否仍足以保障從未同意出現在他人內容中的途人。

causes.label: Livestreaming as a Grassroots Income Hustle
causes.label_zh: 直播作為草根創作者的搵食手段
causes.text: For many small creators, filming ordinary city life is less about artistry than survival, since followers and tips can translate directly into income. That pressure helps explain why some streamers keep recording after being asked to stop, raising how far monetisation should override other people's basic comfort in public.
causes.text_zh: 對許多小型創作者而言，拍攝城市日常生活與其說是藝術創作，更貼近一種求生手段，因為粉絲數字及打賞往往能直接轉化為收入。這種經濟壓力有助解釋，為何部分直播主即使被要求停止，仍繼續拍攝，由此引申出一個問題：將內容變現的考量，應在多大程度上凌駕於他人在公共場所的基本自在？

causes.label: Cross-Border Content Norms Colliding on the MTR
causes.label_zh: 跨境內容創作習慣在港鐵碰撞
causes.text: Much of the unease is not only about filming itself but about whose everyday behaviour counts as 'normal' on shared public transport. When creators raised on a different platform ecosystem bring filming habits that feel intrusive to long-time commuters, the friction becomes a small but telling flashpoint for broader anxieties about shifting norms in shared public spaces.
causes.text_zh: 這場不安，並不只是關於拍攝本身，而是關乎港鐵車廂這個共享空間內，怎樣的日常行為才算「正常」。當在不同平台生態下成長的創作者，帶着令本地長期通勤者感到被侵犯的拍攝習慣登上車廂，這種摩擦便成為反映公共空間規範轉變所引發更廣泛焦慮的一個小小、卻具代表性的爆發點。

causes.label: Online Shaming vs Real Regulatory Fixes
causes.label_zh: 網上公審對比真正的監管改革
causes.text: Public shaming can feel satisfying and may deter one individual streamer, but it does little to fix the underlying gap: by-law enforcement on public transport is inconsistent, and most creators who film strangers never face any consequence at all. A counter-argument worth considering is that outrage cycles on social media substitute for, rather than drive, the policy change actually needed.
causes.text_zh: 網上公開指責或許令人感到痛快，亦可能嚇怕個別直播主，但對修補問題根源作用有限：港鐵附例的執法本身並不一致，而大部分拍攝陌生人的創作者根本從未被追究。值得思考的反論是，社交媒體上一輪又一輪的公眾怒火，往往取代了——而非真正推動了——實際所需的政策改革。
